rationale: The randomized non-Parkinson extra-virgin versus refined olive oil study found a 4.22-point adjusted constipation difference favoring the extra-virgin grade. The paper and registry differ on written dosing. Whole-diet Parkinson and dialysis comparisons were inconclusive. The PRIME schedule confirms separate prospective constipation and stool-form measures, with olive oil recommended within the diet and no reported outcomes.

Two registered Parkinson ginger programmes use standardized powder or two extract strengths and have no posted results. Neither gives a separate reported dyskinesia estimate. The accessible adverse-effect review discusses ginger for nausea and dyskinesia in a separate drug context. Prior isolated zingerone results and multicomponent motor studies leave the ground-ginger hypothesis unresolved.

The combined corn-oil and rotenone animal study reached a motor phenotype earlier than rotenone alone, with no phenotype in the oil-only group during observation. The endpoint combined several motor signs and the authors replaced three animals. Existing gavage and mixed-oil models leave a clinical bradykinesia severity contrast for refined corn oil unresolved.

A randomized dried whole thyme trial reported favorable HADS anxiety compared with starch in university students (group-by-time p=.030). The wild-thyme aqueous extract trial reports an inconclusive anxiety-domain difference in a gastrointestinal population and design discrepancies with the linked registry. Extract and essential-oil animal comparisons measure behavioral proxies. The dried-leaf comparison remains the basis of the weak lean, with limited transfer to Parkinson disease.

The fish-versus-olive-oil exercise trial gives inconclusive single- and dual-task stride interactions (p=.753 and .537) with olive oil grade unspecified. PRIME separately plans wearable same-foot and height-normalized stride, with extra-virgin olive oil recommended within a whole diet. Pressing, actual intake and measured outcomes are unresolved.

The registered hemodialysis trial found lower Rome III scores within all three oil groups, with an inconclusive interaction and unverified flaxseed pressing grade. The lipid trial reports few constipation adverse events. A rodent comparison used solvent-extracted oil and wet stool, with a nonmonotonic response. The human oil observations provide a minimal lean against worsening, with transfer to Parkinson disease unresolved.

Baseline Parkinson walking difficulty showed an inverse association with unspecified olive oil. Timed gait comparisons in obesity and sarcopenia were inconclusive and the Parkinson cannabinoid trial used oil in both arms. PRIME plans separate sensor walking speed and a ten-meter walk within a combined pattern and activity trial, with no reported outcome or confirmed cold-pressed olive oil exposure.
